fixture_note: Scenario 3: a high-risk change that widens a service account's permissions and touches a secrets path. Expected outcome REVIEW driven by an unresolved material contradiction between the test evidence and the security review, with authorization PENDING_CASA because a merge was requested and no CASA authorization was supplied.

intake.problem_statement: A pull request widens the deployment service account from read-scoped to write-scoped and adds a new handler that reads customer records from a secrets-backed configuration path.
constraints: release window closes in six hours
no production data may be used for testing

options.label: Merge the change as submitted
options.mechanism: Accept the widened service account scope and the new configuration handler exactly as written and release inside the current window.
options.tradeoff: Grants a standing write and secrets-read scope that no rollback removes automatically.

options.label: Merge with a request-scoped short-lived credential
options.mechanism: Replace the standing grant with a credential issued per deployment request and expiring at the end of it, keeping the handler otherwise unchanged.
options.tradeoff: Adds a credential-issuance dependency to every deployment and costs one extra release cycle to implement.

evidence_register.locator: pipeline run 9912: 248 tests passing, coverage 87 percent
evidence_register.claim_supported: The change passes the existing automated suite.

evidence_register.locator: DiffWall scan: HALT on sensitive-files rule, REVIEW on auth-and-secrets rule
evidence_register.claim_supported: Change-time scanning flags the secrets path and the permission widening.

evidence_register.locator: security reviewer note: standing write scope is not required by the handler
evidence_register.claim_supported: The widened scope exceeds what the change needs.

evidence_register.locator: svc-deployer credential lifetime is currently unbounded
evidence_register.claim_supported: The existing credential does not expire.

evidence_register.locator: internal standard: deployment credentials must be request-scoped
evidence_register.claim_supported: A request-scoped credential is the standard-conformant pattern.

evidence_register.locator: six hours remain in the release window
evidence_register.claim_supported: Implementation time inside this window is constrained.

assumptions: The handler's stated data requirements are complete.

primitives.statement: The handler needs to read a configuration value backed by a secrets store.
The handler does not itself perform any write to the deployment target.
The existing service credential has no expiry.
Whether any other consumer depends on the standing write scope is unknown.

claims.statement: The write scope in the change is not required by any behaviour the change introduces, so a request-scoped credential satisfies the same functional requirement.

assumptions: The identity provider can issue short-lived credentials without a new integration.

feedback_loops.effect: A widened credential scope propagates into the billing consumer through the records store, and the balancing return path only throttles deployments after the incorrect data has already been consumed.

claims.statement: A standing scope propagates through the records store into a downstream consumer before the balancing path can react, so scope duration is the control point rather than scope correctness.

assumptions: Rejecting the change outright is out of scope for this review.

options.label: Merge the change as submitted
options.mechanism: Accept the widened service account scope and the new configuration handler exactly as written and release inside the current window.
options.tradeoff: Grants a standing write and secrets-read scope that no rollback removes automatically.

options.label: Merge with a request-scoped short-lived credential
options.mechanism: Replace the standing grant with a credential issued per deployment request and expiring at the end of it, keeping the handler otherwise unchanged.
options.tradeoff: Adds a credential-issuance dependency to every deployment and costs one extra release cycle to implement.

options.label: Split the change and ship the handler alone
options.mechanism: Land only the configuration handler behind a feature flag and defer every permission modification to a separate reviewed change.
options.tradeoff: Leaves the handler inert until a second change lands, so no user-visible value ships in this window.

claims.statement: Three mechanisms are available: accept the standing grant, bound the grant in time, or separate the permission change from the functional change.

defects.statement: A passing suite is evidence about behaviour, not about permission scope; no test in the suite exercises the widened credential.
defects.remediation: Add a test that asserts the effective credential scope at deployment time, or stop citing the suite as scope evidence.

defects.statement: The change bundles a permission modification with a functional handler, so neither can be reviewed or reverted independently.
defects.remediation: Separate the permission change into its own reviewable change.

defects.statement: Concluding that no other consumer needs the write scope overstates what the security note establishes, which covers this handler only.
defects.remediation: Enumerate current consumers of the write scope before removing it.

claims.statement: Removing the standing scope is asserted to be safe on the basis of a review that examined only this handler, so the scoped option carries an unquantified regression risk for other consumers.
Merging as submitted bundles an irreversible permission grant with a functional change, which the change-time scan already routes away from automatic acceptance.

failure_modes.statement: The standing secrets-read scope is never revoked, and a later unrelated change reuses the same service account to reach customer records.
failure_modes.precondition: No scheduled review removes the grant after this release.
failure_modes.detection_signal: The service account appears in access logs for resources unrelated to deployment.

failure_modes.statement: Credential issuance becomes a deployment dependency and an issuance outage blocks all releases.
failure_modes.precondition: The identity provider has no fallback issuance path.
failure_modes.detection_signal: Deployment failures correlate with identity provider latency.

failure_modes.statement: The handler ships behind a flag and is forgotten, leaving dead code that later readers assume is active.
failure_modes.precondition: The follow-up permission change is never scheduled.
failure_modes.detection_signal: The feature flag remains off for more than two release cycles.

claims.statement: The only irreversible failure mode in this change belongs to merging as submitted, because a standing grant persists after any code rollback.

effects.statement: A standing grant issued under release pressure becomes the reference precedent for the next urgent change, so the exception rate rises rather than staying constant.
effects.follows_from: The permission widening is accepted inside the release window.

effects.statement: Once deployments depend on issued credentials, credential expiry becomes a monitored signal, which surfaces scope drift that is currently invisible.

claims.statement: Bounding the credential in time converts an invisible standing risk into a monitored signal, which compounds in value across later changes.
